scope: Read-only comparison of already collected ordinary device date/UI evidence; no device commands, source analysis, fault records or rejected-task continuation.
findings: T61B and T72 successful feed observations have surrounding ordinary device dates in 2026; T72 feed file mtime is also 2026.
T68 failed first launch also has ordinary device dates in 2026. Correct-looking date is therefore not sufficient for feed success.

T75 C3/w1 reports Jan 1 1970, a distinct observed system-readiness difference after the user-confirmed power cycle. This audit has not measured real-time clock behavior, synchronization configuration, certificate validation, or their effects.
No crash ownership or causal explanation follows from this comparison; it does not establish that correcting the date fixes the white screen.

System date strings from different boots cannot directly measure cross-run elapsed latency. Use host-side start/end receipts or monotonic uptime within the same boot, preserving exact supply-on time uncertainty.
T72 approximately 63.02 seconds combines host click timing and device image mtime with no independently measured clock offset; retain that precision limitation.

application_scope_limits.T61B: Feed observation only; content operation later failed.
application_scope_limits.T72: One same-boot icon recovery, not physical power first launch or stable use.
application_scope_limits.T75C: User-confirmed physical operation plus changed boot supports the power-cycle observation; accurate physical off/on instants/duration unknown. First ordinary UITest click remained white through120 seconds.
application_scope_limits.T76: Separate normal Settings time-readiness observation only; no extra Toutiao tap authorized by this comparison.

writes: Only this report file; no other files modified by this comparison.
